title: GDPR privacy programme
description: A GDPR programme on the GDPR requirement library: records of processing, data subject requests with their deadlines, personal data breaches with the 72-hour clock, DPIAs, processors and DPAs, transfers outside the EEA and a retention schedule with retention rules; Full adds consent records and the DPO and training. Example items start with "Example:". Retention periods are suggestions: each workspace sets its own.

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: Records of processing, data subject requests, personal data breaches, DPIAs, processors and DPAs, transfers and the retention schedule.

levels.name: Full
levels.description: Everything in Starter plus consent records and the DPO and training.

sheets.name: Records of processing
sheets.description: Your record of processing activities: one item per purpose for which you use personal data, whether you are the controller or a processor for someone else. Keep it current: it is the first thing a supervisory authority asks for.

fields.name: Purpose
fields.description: Why you use the data, in a sentence a member of the public would understand.

fields.name: Legitimate interests assessment
fields.description: Only for legitimate interests: the interest, why the processing is needed and why it does not override the people's rights.

fields.name: Condition for special categories
fields.description: Only when health, biometric, beliefs or other special categories are used: the condition you rely on.

fields.name: Recipients
fields.description: Who receives the data: teams, processors, authorities, other organisations.

fields.name: Security measures
fields.description: A general description of the technical and organisational measures that protect this data.

rules.message: Add the purpose, the lawful basis and the business owner before approving.

values.purpose: Pay staff, deduct tax and social security and keep the records the law asks for.
values.recipients: Payroll provider, tax authority, pension provider
values.security: Access limited to HR and finance; the provider is certified to ISO/IEC 27001; payslips are sent through the provider's portal.

values.purpose: Send news about our products to people who asked for it.
values.security: Double opt-in, unsubscribe link in every email, access limited to marketing.

values.purpose: Protect staff and stock at the warehouse.
values.li_assessment: Theft and safety incidents happened twice last year; cameras cover entrances only; footage is kept 30 days.

sheets.name: Data subject requests
sheets.description: Requests from people to see, correct, delete, restrict, move or object to the use of their data. Answer within one month of receiving the request; you may extend by up to two further months for complex or numerous requests if you tell the person within the first month and say why. The deadline is calculated for you. Log new requests through the form "Submit a data subject request" (Forms tab).

fields.name: Details to find their data
fields.description: What the person told you so you can find their data: customer number, dates, the systems they used.

fields.name: How the identity was checked
fields.description: Say how, never copy the document itself.

rules.message: Say why the request needs more time and when you told the person.

fields.name: Person told about the extension on
Deadline

fields.description: One month from receipt, plus the extension when there is one.

fields.name: Our answer and what we did
Why we refused
fields.description: When refusing: the reason, and that the person may complain to the supervisory authority and go to court.

rules.message: Record the outcome and the answer you gave before closing.

rules.name: Requests: 3 years after closing
rules.note: A suggestion, not advice: set the period your workspace needs (for example the time limit for claims where you are). Erases the requester's details, their files and the comments; the type, dates and outcome stay so you can show how you answered.

values.requester_details: Customer since 2021, orders through the web shop.
values.verified_how: Replied from the email address on the account

values.response: Account and order history deleted; invoices kept for the tax period, which we explained.

sheets.name: Personal data breaches
sheets.description: Every personal data breach, also the ones you decide not to report: the record of what happened, its effects and what you did is required either way. Report to the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people; tell the people affected without undue delay when the risk to them is high. The clock starts at "We became aware at" and stops at "Reported to the authority at". Report new breaches through the form "Report a personal data breach" (Forms tab).

options.label: Lost or stolen device or paper
Data lost or destroyed by mistake

fields.name: What we did to contain it

options.label: Unlikely to result in a risk

fields.name: Why we assessed the risk this way
Reasons for reporting late
fields.description: Required by law when the report is made after 72 hours.

rules.message: Record the containment, the risk and why, and the decisions to report and to tell people before closing.

items.name: Example: payslips emailed to the wrong person

values.description: Five payslips were attached to an email sent to the wrong colleague, who deleted it at once.
values.containment: Recipient confirmed deletion in writing the same day.
values.risk_reasoning: Salary data seen by one colleague, deleted within the hour; no further spread.
values.no_notice_reason: Risk not high: one internal recipient, deletion confirmed.
values.lessons: Payslips now go through the payroll portal only.

layout.title: Report a personal data breach
layout.description: Report at once anything that may have exposed, lost, changed or destroyed personal data: an email to the wrong person, a lost laptop, a break-in. Do not wait until you are sure. The clock for telling the authority may already be running.

fields.label: What caused it, as far as you know?
What kind of data is involved?
About how many people are affected?
What has been done so far?

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The breach lead has your report and will contact you.

sheets.name: DPIAs
sheets.description: Data protection impact assessments for processing likely to result in a high risk to people: describe the processing, why it is needed, the risks and the measures, ask the DPO for advice, and consult the supervisory authority first when a high risk remains.

options.label: Special categories on a large scale

fields.name: Prior consultation with the authority
fields.description: Needed when a high risk remains after the measures.

rules.message: Add the risks, the measures, the risk that remains, the DPO's advice and the decision before approving.

values.description: Cameras at the warehouse entrances with software that matches faces against a list of banned visitors.
values.risks: Staff and visitors monitored without expecting it; wrong matches; footage misused.
values.measures: Signs at every entrance; matching off by default; footage kept 30 days; access logged.

sheets.name: Processors and DPAs
sheets.description: Everyone who handles personal data on your behalf, with the data processing agreement that binds them. Tick what the agreement covers: anything missing is a gap to close with the processor.

options.label: Help with security, breaches and DPIAs
Delete or return the data at the end

fields.name: Sub-processors
fields.description: Who they use, where, and how they tell you about changes.

rules.message: Record when the DPA was signed and when to review it before approving the processor.

sheets.name: Transfers outside the EEA
sheets.description: Personal data sent to, or reachable from, countries outside the EEA, with the mechanism that makes each transfer lawful and your assessment of the destination.

fields.name: Transfer risk assessment
fields.description: What the law and practice of the destination mean for the data, and your conclusion.

rules.message: Name the country and the transfer mechanism before approving.

items.name: Example: email service provider in the United States

sheets.name: Retention schedule
sheets.description: How long you keep each kind of record and why. The schedule says the policy; the retention rules in each sheet's settings (Sheet settings › Retention) apply it: due records go to Workspace admin › Retention, where an owner or admin approves the erasure. Periods shipped here are suggestions: set your own.

fields.name: Retention period
fields.description: For example "3 years after the request is closed".

fields.name: Why this period
fields.description: The law, contract or need that sets it.

fields.name: Applied by
fields.description: The sheet and its retention rule that apply this period, or how it is done elsewhere.

values.period: 3 years after the request is closed
values.why: Long enough to answer a complaint about how the request was handled. Check the time limits that apply to you.
values.applied_by: Data subject requests › Sheet settings › Retention › Requests: 3 years after closing

values.period: Set by tax and employment law where you operate
values.applied_by: The payroll provider, under the DPA

sheets.name: Consent records
sheets.description: Proof of consent where consent is your lawful basis: who agreed, to what, when, how and with which wording, and when they withdrew. Withdrawing must be as easy as giving consent.

fields.name: Wording version
fields.description: The version of the consent text the person saw.

rules.name: Consent: 2 years after withdrawal
rules.note: A suggestion, not advice: keep proof as long as you may need to show the consent was valid, then erase.

sheets.name: DPO and training
sheets.description: Who your data protection officer or privacy contact is, how to reach them and that they report to the highest level of management, and the privacy training people have had and are due.

fields.name: Published contact
fields.description: The address people and the authority use to reach the DPO.

values.audience: Everyone with access to customer or staff data

setup.title: GDPR setup
setup.description: Eight steps to a privacy programme you can show to a supervisory authority. Each step's progress comes from your sheets.

steps.title: Record your processing
steps.body: List each purpose for which you use personal data, with the lawful basis, whose data it is, who receives it and a business owner. Approve each record.

steps.title: Sign a DPA with every processor
steps.body: List the suppliers that handle personal data for you, check what each agreement covers and set a review date.

steps.title: Check your transfers
steps.body: For every processor or recipient outside the EEA, record the country, the mechanism and your assessment.

steps.title: Decide how long you keep data
steps.body: Agree a period for each kind of record, then set the matching retention rules in each sheet's settings. Due records come to Workspace admin › Retention for approval.

steps.title: Be ready for requests from people
steps.body: Open the form "Submit a data subject request", check its questions, write its privacy notice and tell the people who receive requests where to log them.

steps.title: Be ready for breaches
steps.body: Open the form "Report a personal data breach", name a breach lead and tell everyone to report at once, however small.

steps.title: Assess high-risk processing
steps.body: Every processing record marked "DPIA needed" gets an approved DPIA with the DPO's advice.

steps.title: Mark the GDPR articles that apply
steps.body: In the GDPR requirements library, mark each article applicable or not, with a reason, and set its implementation status.
